```{r}
#| label: filter-data

# filter the data
# create final dataset to use

school_safety <- school_safety |>
  select(
    SCHID, # Unique school identifier
    INCPOL18, # Total number of incidents reported to police
    FR_URBAN, # Urbanicity - Based on urban-centric location of school
    FR_SIZE, # Size of school
    C0110:C0186, # School Practices and Programs 
    C0600,
    C0604:C0608,
    C0190:C0192,
    C0204:C0218,
    C0610:C0650,
    C0661,
    C0667,
    # Staff Training
    OUTSUS18, # suspensions
    # C0183, # Social emotional learning training for students
    # C0181, # Individual mentoring/tutoring/coaching by adults
    # C0179, # Student involvement in restorative circles
    # C0186, # Promote sense of community/social integration
    # C0604, # LGBTQ acceptance group
    # C0606, # Disability acceptance group
    # C0608, # Cultural diversity acceptance group 
    # C0190, # Formal process to obtain parental input
    # C0192, # Provide training or assistance to parents
    # C0204, # Community involvement - parent groups
    # C0206, # Community involvement - social services
    # C0208, # Community involvement - juvenile justice
    # C0210, # Community involvement - law enforcement
    # C0212, # Community involvement - mental health
    # C0214, # Community involvement - civic organizations
    # C0216, # Community involvement - businesses
    # C0218, # Community involvement - religious organizations
    C0266, # Teacher training - classroom management
    C0268, # Teacher training - discipline policies related to violence
    C0265, # Teacher training - discipline policies related to cyberbullying
    C0267, # Teacher training - discipline policies related to bullying
    C0269, # Teacher training - alcohol/drug discipline policy
    C0270, # Teacher training - safety procedures
    C0272, # Teacher training - early warning signs for violent behavior
    C0278, # Teacher training - signs of self-harm or suicidal tendencies
    C0271, # Teacher training - intervention and referral strategies
    C0273, # Teacher training - recognize bullying behavior
    C0274, # Teacher training - student alcohol/drug abuse
    C0276, # Teacher training - positive behavioral intervention
    C0277, # Teacher training - crisis prevention and intervention
    # C0610, # Sworn law enforcement officers at school
  )


school_safety <- school_safety |>
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("C")), ~ str_replace(., "2", "0")) |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("C"), as.numeric)) |>
  mutate(resource_sum = 
           C0183 + C0181 + C0179 + C0186 + C0604 + C0606 + C0608 + C0190 + C0192 + C0204 + C0206 + C0208 + 
           C0210 + C0212 + C0214 + C0216 + C0218 + C0266 + C0268 + C0265 + C0267 + C0269 + C0270 + C0272 + 
           C0278 + C0271 + C0273 + C0274 + C0276 + C0277 + C0610
  ) |>
  #mutate(resource_sum = rowSums(across(starts_with("C")))) |>
  arrange(resource_sum) 
  #mutate(across(starts_with("C"), as.logical))

```

```{r}
#| label: linear_regressions_for_each_resource

name <- colnames(school_safety |>
  select(starts_with("C")))

# name <- c("C0183", "C0181" ,  "C0179" ,  "C0186" ,  "C0604" ,  "C0606" ,  "C0608" ,  "C0190" ,  "C0192" , "C0204",
#           "C0206" ,  "C0208" ,  "C0210" ,  "C0212" ,  "C0214" ,  "C0216" ,  "C0218" ,  "C0266" , "C0268" , "C0265",
#           "C0267" ,  "C0269" ,  "C0270" ,  "C0272" ,  "C0278" ,  "C0271" ,  "C0273" ,  "C0274" ,  "C0276" ,
#           "C0277", "C0610")

# fits a model to each of the variables
# resources_fit <- linear_reg() |>
#   fit(INCPOL18 ~ C0183 + C0181 + C0179 + C0186 + C0604 + C0606 + C0608 + C0190 + C0192 + 
#            C0204 + C0206 + C0208 + C0210 + C0212 + C0214 + C0216 + C0218 + C0266 + C0268 +
#            C0265 + C0267 + C0269 + C0270 + C0272 + C0278 + C0271 + C0273 + C0274 + C0276 +
#            C0277 + C0610, 
#       data = school_safety) 

# calculate each of the r coefficients 
cor_coefficients <- sapply(name, function(variable) {
  cor(school_safety[[variable]], school_safety$INCPOL18)
})

# create a vector to store all the values of the r-squared coefficients
r_squared_values <- numeric()
slope <- numeric()

# calculate all the r_squared values for every resource
for (variable in name) {
  # Fit a simple linear regression model for each predictor variable
  lm_model <- lm(school_safety$INCPOL18 ~ school_safety[[variable]])

  # Calculate the R-squared value
  r_squared <- summary(lm_model)$r.squared
  
  tidy_slope <- tidy(lm_model)|>
    filter(term != "(Intercept)")
  slope_value <- tidy_slope$estimate

  # Append values to the vectors
  slope <- c(slope, slope_value)
  r_squared_values <- c(r_squared_values, r_squared)
}

# calculate all the slopes for each resource regression
# slopes <- tidy(resources_fit) |>
#   filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
#   pull(estimate)

# assign all vectors to the resource regression dataframe
resource_regressions2 <- data.frame(name = name, slope = slope, rVAl = cor_coefficients, r_squared_val = r_squared_values)

```

```{r}
total_schools <- nrow(school_safety)
```

```{r}

  filter(FR_URBAN == 1)

# calculate city value box
average_incidents_city <- round(mean(school_safety_city$INCPOL18), digits = 1)

average_resource_score_city <- round(mean(school_safety_city$resource_sum), digits = 1)

total_schools_city <- nrow(school_safety_city)

# filter data for suburban
school_safety_suburban <- school_safety |>
  filter(FR_URBAN == 2) 

# calculate suburb value box 
average_incidents_suburban <- round(mean(school_safety_suburban$INCPOL18), digits = 1)

average_resource_score_suburban <- round(mean(school_safety_suburban$resource_sum), digits = 1)

total_schools_suburban <- nrow(school_safety_suburban)

# filter data for town 
school_safety_town <- school_safety |>
  filter(FR_URBAN == 3)

# calculate town value box
average_incidents_town <- round(mean(school_safety_town$INCPOL18), digits = 1)

average_resource_score_town <- round(mean(school_safety_town$resource_sum), digits = 1)

total_schools_town <- nrow(school_safety_town)

# filter for rural 
school_safety_rural <- school_safety |>
  filter(FR_URBAN == 4)

# calculate rural value box
average_incidents_rural <- round(mean(school_safety_rural$INCPOL18), digits = 1)

average_resource_score_rural <- round(mean(school_safety_rural$resource_sum), digits = 1)

total_schools_rural <- nrow(school_safety_rural)
```

# Home

## Column

```{r}
#| label: scatter plot resources v. incidents all schools
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The graph is a jittered scatter plot titled, “Effect of School on
#|   Incidents Reported to Police.” The x axis is “Amount of School
#|   Resources (out of 30)” and the y axis is “Total Number of Incidents
#|   Reported to the Police.” The x-axis ranges from 0 to 30, and the y
#|   axis ranges from 0 to about 350. The points are clustered close to
#|   the x axis, with most of the points being below 100 incidents
#|   reported to police, though there are some outliers above this line.
#|   There are also more points clustered between 10 and 30 school
#|   resources compared to below 10 and over 30. There appears to be a
#|   slight positive trend, with incidents reported to police increasing as
#|   amount of school resources increases, though it is very slight and
#|   difficult to discern. The shape of the distribution is a very slight left skew.

# all schools
school_safety |>
  ggplot(aes(x = resource_sum, y = INCPOL18)) +
  geom_jitter() +
  labs(
    title = "Effect of School Resources on Incidents Reported to Police", 
    x = "Amount of School Resources (out of 30)",
    y = "Total Number of Incidents Reported to the Police"
  ) 

```

```{r}
scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdPu") +
```

```{r}
#| label: Graph of the resource regressions

regression_plot <- ggplot(resource_regressions2, aes(x = name, y = slope, fill = rVAl)) + 
  geom_col() + 
  scale_fill_distiller(type = "div", limits = c(-.5, .5)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


```

```{r}
#| label: interactive-plot
#| title: School Resources and Practices
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The graph is a bar plot titled, “School Resources and Practices Impact
#|   on Incidents Reported to Police.” The x axis contains the variable
#|   names of 89 school resources, while the y axis is the slope of each
#|   variable. Each variable has its own colored bar that visualizes its
#|   slope compared to the other variables. Most of the variables have
#|   slopes between 0 and 10, although there are 11 variables with negative
#|   slopes, and three variables with slopes above 10. When the cursor of
#|   the computer is hovered over a bar, the variable name and slope will
#|   appear. The four variables with clearly strong slopes are C0134, with a
#|   slope of -3.966, C0153, with a slope of -6.324, C0604, with a slope of
#|   14.595, and C0610, with a slope of 12.814. The colors of the bars
#|   correlate to the R-values of the variables, with a scale ranging from
#|   purple to yellow visualizing this. Variables with the lowest R-values
#|   are colored purple, while variables with the highest R-values are
#|   colored yellow, with blues and greens visualizing the more average 
#|   R-values in between.


plot_ly(data = resource_regressions2, x = ~name, y = ~slope, type = 'bar', 
                            text = ~paste("Variable: ", name, "<br>Slope: ", slope),
                            hoverinfo = 'text', marker = list(color = ~rVAl, colorscale = 'Viridis')) |>
  layout(title = "School Resources and Practices Impact on Incidents Reported to Police")
```

# C0604: LGBTQ Acceptance Groups

## Column

```{r}
#| label: LGBTQ Acceptance Groups - Vary with Incidents
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The graph is a bar plot titled, “LGBTQ Acceptance Groups and Incidents
#|   Reported to Police.” The x axis is “Presence of LGBTQ Acceptance
#|   Groups” with the left bar labeled “No” and the right bar labeled “Yes.”
#|   The y axis is “Incidents Reported to Police” and ranges from 0 to a
#|   little above 20000. The left bar, the “No” bar, is filled in to just
#|   below 12500, at about 12000, and the right bar, the “Yes” bar, is
#|   filled in to just above 20000, at about 22000. The bars are different
#|   colors to provide contrast. 


school_safety <- school_safety |>
  mutate(C0604 = as.factor(C0604))

schoolsaf <- school_safety |>
  group_by(C0604) |>
  summarize(average_incidents_per_school = mean(INCPOL18))

schoolsaf |>
  ggplot(aes(x = C0604, y = average_incidents_per_school, fill = C0604)) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("No", "Yes")) +
  geom_col()
```

## Column {.tabset}

```{r}
#| label: LGBTQ Groups - Vary with Size
#| title: School Size
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The graph is a segmented bar plot titled, “Impact of LGBTQ Acceptance
#|   Groups on Incidents Reported to Police by School Size.” The x axis is
#|   “School Size,” with four different categories: “> 300,” “300 - 499,”
#|   “500 - 999,” and “1000+.” The y axis is “Percentage of Incidents
#|   Reported to Police” and ranges from 0.00 to 1.00. Color is used in this
#|   plot to represent “Presence of LGBTQ Acceptance Groups.” For each of
#|   the school size categories, there is a full bar going from 0.00 - 1.00,
#|   with the bottom of the bar being blue, to represent “Yes,” and the top
#|   of the bar being red to represent “No.” This visualizes each school
#|   size category’s proportion of incidents reported to police based on
#|   whether or not LGBTQ Acceptance Groups are present. The blue portion of
#|   the left-most bar, the “> 300” bar, goes from 0.00 to about 0.35. The
#|   red portion of this bar goes from about 0.35 to 1.00. The blue portion
#|   of the second bar from the left, the “300 - 499” bar, goes from 0.00 to
#|   about 0.20 and the red portion goes from about 0.20 to 1.00. The blue
#|   portion of the third bar from the left, the “500 - 999” bar, goes from
#|   0.00 to about 0.30 and the red portion goes from about 0.30 to 1.00.
#|   The blue portion of the most-right bar, the “1000+” bar, goes from 0.00
#|   to about 0.85, and the red portion goes from about 0.85 to 1.00.


# size graph
ggplot(school_safety, aes(x = FR_SIZE, y = INCPOL18, fill = C0604)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    title = "Impact of LGBTQ Acceptance Groups on Incidents Reported to
       Police By School Size",
    x = "School Size",
    y = "Incidents Reported to Police",
    fill = "Presence of LGBTQ Acceptance Groups"
  ) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("No", "Yes"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The graph is a segmented bar plot titled, “Impact of Required School
#|   Uniforms on Incidents Reported to Police by School Urbanicity.” The x
#|   axis is “Urbanicity,” with four different categories: “City,” “Suburb,”
#|   “Town,” and “Rural.” The y axis is “Percentage of Incidents Reported to
#|   Police” and ranges from 0.00 to 1.00. Color is used in this plot to
#|   represent “Required School Uniforms.” For each of the school size
#|   categories, there is a full bar going from 0.00 - 1.00, with the bottom
#|   of the bar being blue, to represent “Yes,” and the top of the bar being
#|   red to represent “No.” This visualizes each school urbanicity
#|   category’s proportion of incidents reported to police based on whether
#|   or not School Uniforms are required. The blue portion of the left-most
#|   bar, the “City” bar, goes from 0.00 to about 0.18. The red portion of
#|   this bar goes from about 0.18 to 1.00. The blue portion of the second
#|   bar from the left, the “Suburb” bar, goes from 0.00 to about 0.10 and
#|   the red portion goes from about 0.10 to 1.00. The blue portion of the
#|   third bar from the left, the “Town” bar, goes from 0.00 to about 0.11
#|   and the red portion goes from about 0.11 to 1.00. The blue portion of
#|   the most-right bar, the “Rural” bar, goes from 0.00 to about 0.06, and
#|   the red portion goes from about 0.06 to 1.00.

#urbanicity graph
ggplot(school_safety, aes(x = FR_URBAN, y = INCPOL18, fill = C0134)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    title = "Impact of Mandatory School Uniforms on Incidents Reported to
    Police By School Urbanicity",
    x = "Urbanicity",
    y = "Incidents Reported to Police",
    fill = "Mandatory School Uniforms"
  ) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("No", "Yes"))

```

# C0153: Cell Phones Prohibition

## Column

```{r}
#| label: Behavioral Modification for Students - Vary with Incidents

school_safety <- school_safety |>
  mutate(C0153 = as.factor(C0153))

schoolsaf <- school_safety |>
  group_by(C0153) |>
  summarize(average_incidents_per_school = mean(INCPOL18))

schoolsaf |>
  ggplot(aes(x = C0153, y = average_incidents_per_school, fill = C0153)) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("No", "Yes")) +
  geom_col()

```

## Column {.tabset}

```{r}
#| label: Behavioral Modification for Student - Vary with Size

# size graph

  labs(
    title = "Impact of Behavioral Modifications for Students on Incidents
    Reported to Police By School Size",
    x = "School Size",
    y = "Incidents Reported to Police",
    fill = "Behavioral Modifications for Students"
  ) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("No", "Yes"))

```
